title: Ananda Shrestha
profile: Judge of the Kathmandu District Court who issued the five-day remand order for Oli and Lekhak on 29 March 2026.

title: Anil Kumar Sinha
profile: Former Supreme Court justice (1 August 2016-31 October 2023). Minister in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 to 27 March 2026, holding law, justice and parliamentary affairs and several other portfolios.

title: Antonio Guterres
profile: UN Secretary-General. A statement attributed to his spokesperson on 9 September 2025 expressed sadness at the loss of life in Nepal.

title: Anup Kumar Upadhyay
profile: Chief of the Ujyaalo Nepal Party, which announced unity with the RSP on 29 December 2025 and split from it on 10 January 2026.

title: Apilraj Bohora
profile: Kathmandu Police spokesperson (SP) at the time. Said before the protest that forces were on high alert and violators would face action.

title: Arzu Rana Deuba
profile: Nepali Congress. Foreign Minister from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025. Wikipedia reports that she and Sher Bahadur Deuba were injured and taken into police custody after their house was attacked and set on fire on 9 September 2025.

title: Asheem Man Singh Basnyat
profile: Then managing director of Pathao. Onlinekhabar reports he posted on the afternoon of Saturday 6 September 2025 that he would go to Maitighar on 8 September, and an intelligence report listed him as a possible participant.

title: Ashok Raj Sigdel
profile: Chief of the Army Staff since 9 September 2024; appointed on the Council of Ministers' recommendation and announced on 28 August 2024, succeeding Prabhu Ram Sharma. Wikipedia credits him with facilitating the dialogue between Gen Z protest leaders and the political leadership in September 2025.

title: Baburam Aryal
profile: Digital-law expert quoted in Nepali Times criticising the Social Media Bill as placing freedom of expression under criminal law.

title: Baburam Bhattarai
profile: Prime Minister 29 Aug 2011-14 Mar 2013; Finance Minister 2008-2009. Founded the Naya Shakti Party in 2016. Chairman of the Pragatisheel Loktantrik Party from 20 November 2025 (Wikipedia).

title: Baburam Regmi
profile: Former High Court judge who headed the committee that reported on 1 October 2026 on criminal cases against Gen Z protesters.

title: Bala Nanda Sharma
profile: Retired Nepal Army lieutenant general who commanded the UN Disengagement Observer Force from 2004. Foreign Minister in the Karki interim government from December 2025 until 27 March 2026, when Shisir Khanal took over.

title: Balendra Shah
profile: Known as Balen. Elected Mayor of Kathmandu as an independent in May 2022; resigned on 18 January 2026 to contest the 5 March 2026 election. Joined the Rastriya Swatantra Party (from 28 December 2025 per Wikipedia), won Jhapa 5 defeating KP Sharma Oli, and was sworn in as Prime Minister on 27 March 2026. The Ministry of Defence and the Prime Minister's Office websites list him as Prime Minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Beh Lih Yi
profile: CPJ Regional Director; quoted in the 4 September 2025 CPJ statement calling for the ban to be rescinded.

title: Bhola Nath Dhungana
profile: President of Digital Rights Nepal. Told AFP, as reproduced by Al Jazeera on 4 September 2025, that the sudden closure directly hits fundamental rights.

title: Bidya Bhattarai
profile: CPN-UML minister of education in the fourth Oli cabinet from 15 July 2024; resigned on 21 April 2025 amid differences with the prime minister and finance minister over teachers' demands, with a health reason also stated.

title: Bidya Devi Bhandari
profile: President of Nepal from 29 October 2015 to 13 March 2023; succeeded by Ram Chandra Paudel. Wikipedia reports that her house in Bhangal, Kathmandu, was burned during the 2025 protests.

title: Bigyan Raj Sharma
profile: Former additional inspector general of police, member of the Karki inquiry commission.

title: Bijay Prasad Mishra
profile: Listed on Wikipedia as president of the Nepal Bar Association (accessed 2026-10-05); the date he took office is not given in the retrieved page.

title: Binod Ghimire
profile: Deputy Inspector General of Police and Nepal Police spokesperson. Gave Nepal Police figures on escaped prisoners and detainees in September 2025.

title: Bishnu Prasad Paudel
profile: CPN (UML). Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister from 15 July 2024. Forced out on 9 September 2025 with Oli (his own Wikipedia page); the Fourth Oli Cabinet page gives 12 September 2025 for the end of his term.

title: Bishowambhar Prasad Shrestha
profile: Chief Justice who led the Supreme Court's extended full bench in the contempt case against sidhakura.com, whose verdict required mandatory registration of online and social media platforms.

title: Bishwa Prakash Sharma
profile: Nepali Congress general secretary. With Gagan Thapa he demanded Home Minister Lekhak's resignation on 8 September 2025 and, on 9 September, that the party recall its ministers from the Oli government.

title: Bishweshwor Prasad Bhandari
profile: Legal expert, member of the Karki inquiry commission.

title: Bishwo Adhikari
profile: Senior Superintendent of Police and Kathmandu police chief on 8 September 2025. The Himalayan Times (10 October 2025) reports testimony that he issued the order to fire; the NHRC later recommended departmental action against a 'Senior SP Bishwa Adhikari'. The accounts are reports of testimony and recommendations, not findings of a court.

title: Biswas Baral
profile: Editor-in-chief of The Kathmandu Post (Wikipedia).

title: Célia Mercier
profile: Head of the RSF South Asia Desk; quoted in the 12 September 2025 RSF statement on attacks on media.

title: Chandra Kuber Khapung
profile: Inspector General of Nepal Police. The cabinet appointed him on 29 August 2025 to replace Deepak Thapa; he assumed office as the 32nd IGP on 4 September 2025, days before the protests. He retired on 12 November 2025 after 30 years of service. The government commission named him, with Oli and Lekhak, for criminal investigation (Onlinekhabar, 25 March 2026).

title: Chandra Prasad Dhakal
profile: President of the Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry. Quoted in September 2025 on private-sector losses of NPR 80 billion and NPR 80 to 100 billion.

title: Chhabi Rijal
profile: Chief District Officer of Kathmandu during the protests of 8-9 September 2025. Arrested from his home in Koteshwor on 31 March 2026 by the Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office after the government commission's recommendation (Himalayan Times). The commission recommended action against him under Section 182 (Onlinekhabar). Deccan Herald's report of the 9 September curfew notice gives his name as 'Chhabilal Rijal'.

title: Chomendra Neupane
profile: Director of the Department of Prison Management. Gave figures on rearrested and returned prisoners in September 2025.

title: Dan Bahadur Karki
profile: Additional IGP at the time of the protests; the NHRC recommended departmental action against him (reported 27 May 2026). Cabinet appointed him Inspector General of Nepal Police on 10 November 2025; Wikipedia lists him as 33rd IGP from 13 November 2025.

title: Deepak Khadka
profile: Energy Minister. Setopati reports his home was vandalised on the morning of 9 September 2025.

title: Deepak Thapa
profile: 31st Inspector General of Nepal Police, 18 March 2025 to 3 September 2025 (Wikipedia list); replaced by Chandra Kuber Khapung, appointed on 29 August 2025.

title: Dev Raj Ghimire
profile: CPN (UML). Speaker of the House of Representatives from 19 January 2023; Wikipedia gives 19 January 2026 as the end of his term. Member for Jhapa 2 until the dissolution on 12 September 2025. Succeeded as Speaker by Dol Prasad Aryal on 5 April 2026.

title: Dharma Raj Bhusal
profile: Founder, owner and president of the Online Khabar news portal (Wikipedia).

title: Dil Bhusan Pathak
profile: Journalist who published claims on his YouTube channel about the business interests of a leading political family; police sought to arrest him in June 2025 according to HRW and CPJ.

title: Dol Prasad Aryal
profile: RSP. Speaker of the House of Representatives since 5 April 2026, succeeding Dev Raj Ghimire. Vice chairperson of the RSP from 2022 to 26 June 2026 and Labour Minister in 2023 and 2024.

title: Durga Prasai
profile: Medical entrepreneur and political activist. Reporting names him as the chief coordinator of the 28 March 2025 pro-monarchy protest at Tinkune; he was arrested in Bhadrapur, Jhapa, on 11 April 2025 on charges of crimes against the state and organised crime. The name is also printed as Prasain in Kantipur.

title: Gagan Thapa
profile: Nepali Congress general secretary 16 Dec 2021-14 Jan 2026; Health Minister 2016-2017. Elected unopposed as party president at the second special general convention (11-14 January 2026); the Election Commission recognised the new leadership on 16 January 2026. Lost the Sarlahi 4 seat in the March 2026 election (Wikipedia).

title: Gajendra Kumar Thakur
profile: Spokesperson of the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology. Quoted on 4 and 5 September 2025 on the deactivation of unregistered platforms and on X asking for registration documents.

title: Gauri Bahadur Karki
profile: Retired Supreme Court judge who chaired the commission that investigated the killings and damage of 8-9 September 2025; he handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki (Kathmandu Post, 8 March 2026).

title: Gokarna Mani Duwadi
profile: Home Secretary at the time of the protests, according to the Onlinekhabar report of 25 March 2026, which says the commission recommended action against him under Section 182.

title: Gyanendra Shah
profile: Last King of Nepal (reigned 2001-2008). In 2025 pro-monarchy crowds gathered around his visits; a rally in Kathmandu on 5 March 2025 backed his possible return (Wikipedia).

title: Hanaa Singer-Hamdy
profile: UN Resident Coordinator in Nepal. Issued a statement of solidarity on 12 September 2025.

title: Harka Sampang
profile: Mayor of Dharan from 23 May 2022 to 19 January 2026, elected as an independent; founder of the Shram Sanskriti Party; won Sunsari-1 in 2026. Reported in the 2025 protests article as Harka Raj Rai, Mayor of Dharan.

title: Hit Raj Pandey
profile: Chief whip of CPN (Maoist Centre) in the 4 September 2025 Kathmandu Post report. He called the shutdown objectionable and warned it could throw the country into disarray.

title: Hutaraj Thapa
profile: Chief of the National Investigation Department at the time. Says written reports on the planned protest were submitted; one dated 7 September 2025 was obtained by Onlinekhabar.

title: Ishwar Pokhrel
profile: Oli's closest competitor in the December 2025 UML chair vote, with 564 votes against Oli's 1,663.

title: Jagdish Kharel
profile: Minister of Communication and Information Technology in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 to 19 January 2026, succeeding Prithvi Subba Gurung; member of the House for Lalitpur 2 since 26 March 2026.

title: Jasmine Ojha
profile: Named in the NHRC report, as reported by HimalPress, among protest coordinators who argued with Sudan Gurung at Maitighar on the morning of 8 September 2025.

title: Jhalanath Khanal
profile: Prime Minister 6 Feb-29 Aug 2011; chairman of CPN (UML) 2009-2014. In the CPN (Unified Socialist) 2021-2025; senior leader of the Nepali Communist Party since 5 November 2025. The Wikipedia article on the 2025 protests lists his residence among the buildings set on fire.

title: Kailash Sirohiya
profile: Chairman of Kantipur Publications (Kantipur Media Group), whose headquarters buildings were attacked in September 2025 according to Wikipedia.

title: Kiran Pokhrel
profile: Spokesman / press adviser to President Ram Chandra Paudel. AP quotes him announcing Karki's appointment on 12 September 2025 (spelled Kiran Pokhrel); Khaleej Times spells the name Kiran Pokharel.

title: KP Sharma Oli
profile: Chairman of CPN-UML (2014-2018; again from 2021). Prime Minister three times: 12 Oct 2015-4 Aug 2016, 15 Feb 2018-13 Jul 2021 and 15 Jul 2024 to September 2025. He resigned on 9 September 2025 during the Gen Z protests; Wikipedia's biography gives 12 September 2025 as the end of the term, the date Sushila Karki took over. After the 5 March 2026 election (he lost Jhapa-5 to Balen Shah, per Wikipedia) he was detained on 28 March 2026 following the recommendation of the government commission on the protest deaths; the Supreme Court declined to release him and Ramesh Lekhak (reported 31 March 2026). The NHRC report held him primarily responsible for the rights violations (reported 27 May 2026).

title: Kulman Ghising
profile: Managing director of the Nepal Electricity Authority 2016-2020 and 2021 until his removal on 24 March 2025. Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as minister of energy, water resources and irrigation, also holding urban development and physical infrastructure in the Karki interim government; resigned 7 January 2026. Chairman of the Ujyaalo Nepal Party from 10 January 2026. Wikipedia lists him among the candidates discussed for interim prime minister.

title: Lin Jian
profile: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson. Commented on Nepal on 10 September 2025.

title: Madan Prasad Pariyar
profile: Climate and agriculture expert, president of the Samata Foundation; named on 21 September 2025 as agriculture minister in the Karki cabinet.

title: Madhav Kumar Nepal
profile: Prime Minister 25 May 2009-6 Feb 2011. Chairman of the CPN (Unified Socialist) from 18 Aug 2021 until its merger on 4 Nov 2025; co-coordinator of the Nepali Communist Party since 5 November 2025.

title: Mahabir Pun
profile: Technologist and social entrepreneur. Minister of Education, Science and Technology in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 until he resigned on 20 January 2026 to contest the election. Won Myagdi-1 as an independent in March 2026 and was assigned the science, technology and innovation portfolio on 9 June 2026 (ShareSansar).

title: Man Bahadur Karki
profile: Chief Election Commissioner of Nepal as listed on Wikipedia (accessed 2026-10-05); the date he took office is not given in the retrieved page.

title: Manbir Rai
profile: CPN (UML). Minister of Defence from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025; member of the House for Solukhumbu 1.

title: Meenakshi Ganguly
profile: Deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch; quoted in the 9 September 2025 HRW release on the police shootings.

title: Min Bahadur Gurung
profile: Chairperson of Bhat-Bhateni Supermarket. Reported company losses of NPR 10.85 billion after the 9 September 2025 attacks on its stores.

title: Narayan Dutta Poudel
profile: Additional Inspector General promoted to Inspector General of the Armed Police Force, scheduled to take office on 1 May 2026 (Kathmandu Post, 27 April 2026). The name is spelled Narayan Datta Paudel on Wikipedia.

title: Narendra Modi
profile: Prime Minister of India. Posted on X on 13 September 2025 wishing Karki well as interim prime minister; Deccan Chronicle reports him calling the appointment a shining example of women empowerment.

title: Nimesh Shrestha
profile: TikTok content creator named by Nepali Times as publicly backing Hami Nepal, and by Onlinekhabar among the prominent voices calling for the 8 September 2025 protest.

title: Nirmala Sharma
profile: Chair of the Federation of Nepali Journalists, quoted in Nepali Times on the Social Media Bill.

title: Om Prakash Aryal
profile: Advocate. Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as Minister of Home Affairs in the Karki interim government, also holding law, justice and parliamentary affairs until 22 September 2025. Home Minister until 26 March 2026; succeeded by Sudan Gurung.

title: Prabhu Ram Sharma
profile: Chief of the Army Staff from 9 September 2021 to 8 September 2024 (Wikipedia); succeeded by Ashok Raj Sigdel. Himal Press says his term ended on 9 September 2024.

title: Pradip Paudel
profile: Health and Population Minister. Announced on 9 September 2025 that he was stepping down. Kantipur lists him as the fourth minister to resign after Lekhak, Chaudhary and Adhikari. Spelled Poudel in some reports.

title: Pradip Yadav
profile: Water Supply Minister and deputy general secretary of the Janata Samajwadi Party. Announced on Facebook on 9 September 2025 that he was resigning in support of the protests and against the crackdown.

title: Prakash Man Singh Raut
profile: Chief Justice of Nepal from 6 October 2024 until his retirement on 31 March 2026, appointed by President Ram Chandra Paudel. Not the same person as Deputy Prime Minister Prakash Man Singh. Followed by Sapana Pradhan Malla as acting Chief Justice.

title: Prem Raj Karki
profile: Former High Court judge who heads the committee formed on 15 April 2026 to study the security agencies' role on 8-9 September.

title: Prithvi Subba Gurung
profile: CPN (UML). Minister of Communication and Information Technology from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025; Chief Minister of Gandaki Province 2018-2021. In April 2025 he said platforms that defied the government's call to register would be banned. The NHRC termed the 2023 directive behind the restriction unconstitutional and recommended action against him (reported 27 May 2026).

title: Pushpa Kamal Dahal
profile: Known as Prachanda. Prime Minister 2008-2009, 2016-2017 and 26 Dec 2022-15 Jul 2024. Chair of the CPN (Maoist Centre) until it merged into the Nepali Communist Party on 4-5 November 2025; coordinator of the Nepali Communist Party since 5 November 2025. Leader of the opposition 15 Jul 2024-12 Sep 2025. Member of the House for Eastern Rukum 1 since 26 March 2026 (Wikipedia).

title: Rabi Lamichhane
profile: Chairperson of the Rastriya Swatantra Party (founded 1 July 2022). Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister 26 Dec 2022-27 Jan 2023 and 6 Mar-15 Jul 2024. Arrested 4 April 2025 in a cooperative fraud case; freed from Nakkhu prison on 9 September 2025 during the protests, returned on 13 September, and released on bail on 19 December 2025 (Wikipedia; release reported by Himal Press). Returned to the RSP headquarters on 21 December 2025 after 261 days.

title: Rajaram Basnet
profile: Brigadier General and Nepali Army spokesperson, named in Setopati's report of the army's 10 pm ultimatum on 9 September 2025.

title: Rajendra Lingden
profile: Chairman of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party since 5 December 2021. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation 17 Jan-25 Feb 2023. Member of the House for Jhapa 3 from 2018 until the dissolution on 12 September 2025.

title: Raju Aryal
profile: Inspector General of the Armed Police Force during the September 2025 protests. The inquiry commission concluded he failed to give proper direction to his force (Ratopati, 26 March 2026) and recommended action against him (Onlinekhabar). He retired compulsorily on 1 May 2026 after a four-year tenure; Narayan Dutta Poudel took over.

title: Rajyalaxmi Chitrakar
profile: Wife of former prime minister Jhalanath Khanal. Injured with burns when the family home in Dallu was set on fire on 9 September 2025. Also written Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar. Some outlets reported her dead on 9 September; fact-checkers and Setopati said she was alive. She returned home after treatment in Delhi in December 2025.

title: Rakshya Bam
profile: Named as one of the coordinators calling themselves Gen Z leaders on 8 September 2025 (NHRC report as reported by HimalPress) and listed by Onlinekhabar among people who later emerged as Gen Z leaders.

title: Ram Bahadur Thapa
profile: CPN-UML vice-chair. In September 2026 he prepared a 39-page report arguing that Oli need not step down after the election defeat.

title: Ram Chandra Paudel
profile: President of Nepal since 13 March 2023, succeeding Bidya Devi Bhandari. Member of the Nepali Congress until 2023, then left active party membership after the presidential election (Wikipedia). Earlier Speaker of the House of Representatives (1994-1999), Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister (2000-2001). In September 2025 he administered the oath to the Karki interim ministers at Shital Niwas.

title: Ram Nath Adhikari
profile: Agriculture and Livestock Development Minister from the Nepali Congress. Resigned on 9 September 2025, saying he acted on moral grounds and to object to the government's actions. Republica reports he stepped down after party leader Shekhar Koirala directed his faction's ministers to quit.

title: Ramesh Lekhak
profile: Nepali Congress politician. Home Minister from 15 July 2024; resigned on 8 September 2025, the day of the police firing, taking 'moral responsibility'. Detained on 28 March 2026 after the government commission recommended a criminal investigation; the Supreme Court declined to release him and Oli (reported 31 March 2026).

title: Rameshwor Khanal
profile: Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as finance minister in the Karki interim government at Shital Niwas. The Kathmandu Post spells his name 'Rameshore Khanal'; the Karki cabinet page on Wikipedia lists 'Rameshwar Khanal' as finance minister until 27 March 2026.

title: Rastra Bimochan Timalsina
profile: Advocate known as "Random Nepali" on YouTube, advising the Gen Z protesters; one of five names shortlisted in the Discord poll. The Wikipedia table spells the name Timalsena.

title: Ravina Shamdasani
profile: OHCHR spokesperson. Called for a prompt and transparent investigation into the Nepal killings on 8-9 September 2025.

title: Sabita Bhandari
profile: Senior advocate whom PM Karki had already appointed Attorney General by 15 September 2025 (Setopati).

title: Sagar Dhakal
profile: Independent politician who ran against Sher Bahadur Deuba in 2022; one of five names shortlisted in the Discord poll and named by the Kathmandu Post as a name in circulation.

title: Samiksha Baskota
profile: Head of the Bibeksheel Sajha Party, which announced its merger with the RSP on 30 November 2025.

title: Sangeeta Mishra
profile: Former additional secretary at the health ministry; the Kathmandu Post reported on 21 September 2025 that the President would appoint her health minister. The ANI report of the 22 September swearing-in lists four ministers and no health minister, and Wikipedia lists Sudha Sharma Gautam as health minister from 26 October 2025.

title: Sapana Pradhan Malla
profile: Justice of the Supreme Court since 1 August 2016; Acting Chief Justice from 1 April to 19 May 2026, after Prakash Man Singh Raut retired.

title: Satyaraj Joshi
profile: Named by Republica as the Prison Administrator whose signature appears on the release letter that Rabi Lamichhane made public. Republica reports he later declined to take ownership of the letter.

title: Shankar Pokharel
profile: CPN-UML general secretary. His 65-page report recommended that Oli take responsibility and step down (as described by Onlinekhabar). At the Nepali Congress convention in October 2026 he asked whether Nepal was moving towards authoritarianism.

title: Shaswot Lamichhane
profile: Described by Green European Journal as an 18-year-old who messaged Hami Nepal on 7 September 2025 about logistics and became a moderator of the Youths Against Corruption Discord server.

title: Shekhar Koirala
profile: Nepali Congress leader. On 8 September 2025 he wrote that the party could not remain in government after the killings, according to Himal Press, and The Kathmandu Post lists him among senior Congress leaders who called for withdrawal.

title: Sher Bahadur Deuba
profile: President of the Nepali Congress from 7 March 2016 to 16 January 2026, when Gagan Thapa was recognised as president. Prime Minister five times, most recently 13 Jul 2021-26 Dec 2022. Leader of the opposition 2022-2024. Wikipedia reports that his residence was attacked and set on fire on 9 September 2025 and that he and his wife, Arzu Rana Deuba, were injured.

title: Shisir Khanal
profile: RSP member for Kathmandu 6. Minister of Foreign Affairs from 27 March 2026; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs website names him as minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Stéphane Dujarric
profile: Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General. Commented on Nepal on 9 September 2025.

title: Sudan Gurung
profile: Founder of Hami Nepal, the youth NGO that called the 8 September 2025 protest and, per Wikipedia, liaised between organisers and the Nepali Army afterwards. Joined the RSP on 18 January 2026, won Gorkha 1 on 9 March 2026, became Home Minister on 27 March 2026, resigned on 22 April 2026 citing moral responsibility amid a controversy over his financial conduct, and was reappointed on 9 June 2026 after an inquiry cleared him (ShareSansar, Wikipedia). The Ministry of Home Affairs website names him as minister (accessed 2026-10-05; Nepali spelling there: Sudhan Gurung).

title: Suman Ghimire
profile: Chief District Officer of Lalitpur. On 9 September 2025 he said the curfew order applied to parts of Lalitpur wards 2, 4, 9, 18 and 25 (Kathmandu Post).

title: Sushila Karki
profile: Former Chief Justice of Nepal (acting from 11 July 2016, retired June 2017). Sworn in as interim Prime Minister on 12 September 2025 and held the office until 27 March 2026; the first woman to be Prime Minister. Wikipedia reports that Gen Z organisers selected her name in an online Discord poll. The House of Representatives was dissolved on 12 September 2025 and elections were set for 5 March 2026. On 8 March 2026 she received the report of the commission headed by Gauri Bahadur Karki.

title: Swarnim Wagle
profile: Economist and vice chairperson of the Rastriya Swatantra Party since 29 November 2023. Finance Minister in the Balen Shah government since 27 March 2026; member for Tanahun 1.

title: Tejulal Chaudhary
profile: Youth and Sports Minister in the Oli cabinet. Resigned on 9 September 2025 after the use of force against the protests.

title: Top Bahadur Magar
profile: Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission, Nepal, 'since 3rd February 2021' according to the commission's website; a former Supreme Court justice (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Upendra Yadav
profile: Chairman of the Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal (the party's English name on Wikipedia is People's Socialist Party, Nepal) since its founding on 22 April 2020. Deputy Prime Minister 1 Jun 2018-24 Dec 2019 and 10 Mar-13 May 2024; Foreign Minister 2008-2009 and 2011. Member of the House from 2 May 2023 until its dissolution on 12 September 2025.

title: Veronique Lorenzo
profile: EU Ambassador to Nepal; welcomed Karki's appointment as first woman PM on 13 September 2025.

title: Volker Türk
profile: Austrian lawyer; UN High Commissioner for Human Rights since 17 October 2022, succeeding Michelle Bachelet. The Wikipedia article on the 2025 protests lists him among the international officials who commented.

title: Yam Lal Kandel
profile: CPN (UML). Chief Minister of Karnali Province from 10 April 2024 to 28 July 2026 (Wikipedia). His residence in Birendranagar was set on fire during the 2025 protests.

title: Yogesh Bhattarai
profile: CPN-UML leader who told a secretariat meeting in May 2026 that the party could not move forward under Oli and that Oli should resign (reported indirectly).
